source_lines: 1418–1427: coordinate legs in a fixed order, their time parameterization and preservation of a containing cube; this prototype handles one local coordinate polyline
review_flags_scope: The actual continuous coordinate polyline on a unit time interval, its finite closed-cell branch formulas, exact endpoints and cube containment. No completed global thm:relgp or multi-coarse-cell path acceptance.
reason: The prototype faithfully implements the local timed coordinate-polyline step. It constructs a continuous function by gluing finitely many genuine continuous branches on the actual closed uniform mesh, proves branch agreement on every intersection, and retains the exact branch formula on every entire cell. The local real time is m*t−j, lies in [0,1] on cell j, and equals 0 and 1 at that cell’s actual endpoints. Each branch is the accepted actual ordered coordinate leg at that local time. Adjacent branches meet at exactly the same ordered hybrid, so the resulting map has exact endpoints x and y. Since the actual closed cells exhaust the unit interval, every map value remains in every scalar cube that contains both endpoints. Equal coordinate steps are allowed; the independent constant-endpoint example confirms the whole map is then constant. A second independent example reconstructs a genuine continuous labelled-tuple map with exact endpoints and full-time preservation of each actual tuple cube containing them. The proof uses only standard axioms and actual finite closed-set gluing, not an assumed global path. This is one local polyline between two given vectors; global source-cell concatenation, synchronization with the original curve, wall-event transport and the complete original theorem remain separate.

mathematical_justification.assessment: For a finite closed cover whose union is all of X, every point has a covering index. Ordinary Classical.choice selects one such index and defines g(x) by the actual corresponding branch value F(index(x))(x). The pairwise agreement hypothesis proves g(x)=F(i)(x) for every covering set containing x, not only for the chosen index. Each restriction is continuous because it agrees with the continuous branch. Finiteness gives local finiteness, and the pinned LocallyFinite.continuous theorem for a closed cover then proves continuity of g. The pinned proof was inspected through its neighborhood-filter union argument. No Hausdorff target, metric target, nonempty index-type assumption or supplied continuous g is introduced. Global branch continuity is stronger than continuity on each piece, but is actually proved for the affine ambient-vector branches used here; no extension into the Regular locus outside a cell is assumed.

mathematical_justification.clause: Exact real local time and its cell bounds
mathematical_justification.assessment: uniformMeshLocalTime N j t is the actual real scalar N*(t:ℝ)−j.val. It is continuous by multiplication by a real constant and subtraction. For t in the genuine closed cell [j/N,(j+1)/N], multiplying the two real inequalities by positive N gives j≤N*t≤j+1. Subtracting j yields local time in [0,1]. At the left and right mesh points, nonzero N allows direct field simplification to 0 and 1. The use of explicit real arithmetic avoids truncated or other arithmetic on the unitInterval subtype.

mathematical_justification.clause: Actual affine branches and exact endpoint hybrids
mathematical_justification.assessment: timedScalarBranch is exactly orderedScalarLeg order x y j composed with local time m*t−j. The inherited orderedScalarLeg is the actual scalar affine line between hybrid j and hybrid j+1, so the formula describes an actual affine branch in source time; it is not an arbitrary supplied per-cell value. Continuity follows by composition of the proved continuous maps. Substituting the exact local endpoint times yields precisely those two endpoint hybrids. The branch may be evaluated outside its own cell as an ambient vector function, but the cube-containment assertion is only used with the proved local parameter in [0,1].

mathematical_justification.clause: Every cell intersection has matching branch values
mathematical_justification.assessment: For i<j and a point in both cells, the independently reviewed intersection theorem forces j=i+1 and identifies the point with the right endpoint of cell i and left endpoint of cell j. The two branch values are therefore hybrid i+1 and hybrid j, equal by that natural-index identity. Trichotomy handles every pair of indices: the forward case uses this theorem, equality is reflexive, and the reverse case is its symmetric version. Thus the finite gluing agreement condition is proved for all intersections, including both orderings and the same-cell case. Shared closed endpoints are retained and handled explicitly.

mathematical_justification.clause: Exact global endpoints of the local polyline
mathematical_justification.assessment: The first mesh cell contains time 0, and its actual branch value there is hybrid 0=x. The last index m−1 is valid under m>0; its successor endpoint is exactly time 1 and its right hybrid index is m, giving y. The gluing formula then proves g(0)=x and g(1)=y as actual scalar-vector equalities. This also covers m=1: the single branch has both correct endpoints. For the source scalar tuple order, n≥3 gives m=2*n>0 without strengthening the source size domain.

mathematical_justification.clause: Full-time preservation of every containing cube
mathematical_justification.assessment: The resulting g is chosen before any cube center or radius. For any scalarOpenBox containing both endpoints and any actual time t, cell exhaustion supplies a j containing t. The gluing equality identifies g(t) with branch j, and the local-time theorem puts its real leg parameter in [0,1]. The inherited ordered-leg containment theorem then places g(t) in that same cube. The conclusion is universal over all such boxes and all times, not merely a sampled or endpoint property. No nonzero step, distinct endpoint vector or polynomial nonvanishing condition is required.

mathematical_justification.clause: Independent zero-step and actual tuple checks
mathematical_justification.assessment: The first independent example takes x=y, obtains the constructed polyline and uses its actual cell formula plus cell exhaustion to prove g(t)=x for every t. This confirms that zero coordinate changes and fixed endpoint collar vectors are permitted. The second takes arbitrary actual labelled tuples P,Q with n≥3, uses the fixed scalarCoordinateOrder, composes the constructed scalar map with the proved continuous tuple reconstruction, and proves exact original labelled endpoints. It transports the universal box assertion through scalarCoordinates_tupleOf to actual tupleScalarBox containment for the whole local path. No source/target quotient or occurrence relabeling is used.

This result supplies one timed coordinate polyline between two given scalar vectors on one unit interval. Its per-cell formula gives the concrete affine pieces, but it does not itself flatten coarse source cells with all their ordered legs, synchronize them with the original source curve, prove a single global Regular approximating path, carry the finite root/event sets through that time change or classify the resulting germs. The separately developing MultiCellCoordinatePolyline prototype is outside this review. No project-level formal piecewise-affine/global-wall statement is accepted merely from this local prototype.
